cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: Leader election lets several replicas of kube-scheduler and kube-controller-manager run for high availability without fighting over the same resources. Only one replica, the leader, does reconciliation work; the others are followers that watch and wait.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: It uses a Lease object (coordination.k8s.io/v1) stored in etcd. The leader keeps renewing the Lease; if it stops, a follower sees it expire and atomically takes it over. Key fields are holderIdentity and leaseDurationSeconds. Unlike kube-apiserver, these components are active-passive, not active-active.

questions.q: Do the scheduler and controller manager run active-active like kube-apiserver?
questions.a: No. They are active-passive: one leader works while the others stand by.
